Seventeen comments

Italian Rant - Italian indeed

This tune is best known as La Mantovana, notated in (among other sources) Il Solaro by Gasparo Zanetti (fl. 1620s - 1645). John Playford included it in several publications, including later editions of The English Dancing-Master. The first section is also related to the principal theme from Smetana’s ‘The Moldau’ and the Israeli National Anthem ‘Hatikvah’.

Why is it here?

Italian Rant

The tune is shown here as in A minor (no sharps or flats and I stand ready to be corrected) but I think it is more commonly played in G minor. We try to play this in our Four Marks Folk Band Sessions. I am told there is a C part to the tune.

It’s a little rude and more than a little intolerant posting rhetorical questions like “why is it here” in response to non-Celtic music, when a contributor has spent time and effort transcribing, researching and posting an interesting tune. This challenging behaviour often pops up here in response to Southern European tunes, which many Subscribers find stimulating and those accompanying international dancers find useful, given the dearth of transcriptions elsewhere. Bravo Alancorsini for starting this post, and the many who added to our understanding of this fascinating tune
